name: Arpa’s letter-marked tree and Mehrdad’s Dokhtar-kosh paths
description: Just in case somebody missed it: we have wonderful girls in Arpa’s land. Arpa has a rooted tree (connected acyclic graph) consisting of n vertices. The vertices are numbered 1 through n , the vertex 1 is the root. There is a letter written on each edge of this tree. Mehrdad is a fan of Dokhtar-kosh things. He call a string Dokhtar-kosh, if we can shuffle the characters in string such that it becomes palindrome. He asks Arpa, for each vertex v , what is the length of the longest simple path in subtree of v that form a Dokhtar-kosh string.
input_specification: The first line contains integer n ( 1  ≤ n ≤  5·10 5 ) — the number of vertices in the tree. ( n -  1) lines follow, the i -th of them contain an integer p i + 1 and a letter c i + 1 ( 1  ≤ p i + 1 ≤ i , c i + 1 is lowercase English letter, between a and v , inclusively), that mean that there is an edge between nodes p i + 1 and i + 1 and there is a letter c i + 1 written on this edge.
output_specification: Print n integers. The i -th of them should be the length of the longest simple path in subtree of the i -th vertex that form a Dokhtar-kosh string.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.
